newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Amnesty condemns verdict for Malaysia opposition MP.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty condemns verdict for Malaysia opposition MP.

text.p: Human rights group Amnesty International has condemned a Malaysian court verdict that found a leading opposition politician guilty of sedition.
On Monday, the High Court in west coast Malacca state found Lim Guan Eng, youth leader of the Democratic Action Party (DAP), guilty on two charges of sedition and spreading false news.

In a statement issued after the verdict, London-based Amnesty, which had previously spoken out in support of Lim, said the case against the DAP member was "politically motivated" and a move by the Malaysian government "to silence a leading critic".
"The case against Lim Guan Eng fits the government's strategy of selectively using repressive laws to discourage dissent," said the Amnesty statement, received in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.
Lim faces the loss of his parliamentary seat, and was fined 15,000 ringgit ($5,976) for violating the Sedition Act and the Printing and Publications Act.

Under article 48 of the Federal Constitution, a member of parliament is disqualified if he is sentenced to a year's jail or a 2,000 ringgit ($800) fine. The disqualification takes effect 14 days from the day of conviction, barring an appeal.
Lim said on Monday he would file an appeal.
Amnesty urged in its statement, "Lim Guan Eng's fine should be revoked and he should not be deprived of his parliamentary seat."
Lim was charged with making false statements in 1995 about Malacca's Chief Minister Rahim Tamby Chik, who was accused by a then 15-year-old schoolgirl of having an affair with her.
Rahim, who was a rising star in Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) as head of that party's youth wing, denied the accusation.
Lim said the girl, kept in police custody for more than a week for investigation of the complaint, was an "imprisoned victim" in the case and Rahim should be in jail instead.
The prosecution contended the statement was seditious because it seemed to accuse police of illegally detaining the girl.

Prime Minister Mahathir, asked on Monday what the court's decision would mean for the opposition, told reporters in Kuala Lumpur: "The message is that our courts are unfair to opposition politicians. That's what the press will read anyway.
"Anything against the government is fair, anything against the opposition is unfair. So what's the good of asking me, you have already made up your mind."
The opposition holds 30 seats in the 192-seat parliament. The DAP with nine seats is the largest opposition party.
